meanings.note: je peux t'appeler? = can I call you?
Je m'appelle Camille. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to call'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'appelé').

examples.text: Appelle Clémentine. Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: Call Clémentine. Tell her I can't come tonight.

meanings.note: Feminine: assistante. Masculine noun ('le assistant', plural 'les assistants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'assistant'.

examples.text: Vous êtes l'assistante de Mathias Barneville?

meanings.note: à + le contracted: au boulot, au téléphone

examples.trans: I've got a problem at work.

meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'with', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.
Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: Same form in the plural. Masculine noun ('le choix', plural 'les choix') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'choice'.

examples.text: Elle est partie avec Mathias. C'est son choix.
examples.trans: She left with Mathias. It's her choice.

meanings.note: Comment ça va?. Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.
Informal. Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.
perdre le contrôle = to lose control
Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard masculine noun meaning 'control; check, inspection'.

examples.text: Vous n'aimez pas perdre le contrôle.
Le contrôle fiscal. Cette lettre pour monsieur Jarron?
examples.trans: The tax audit. That letter for Mr Jarron?

meanings.en: copy (of a text, script, or film)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la copie', plural 'les copies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'copy'.

examples.text: Il y a seulement cent vingt copies distribuées!

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to speak'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'parlé').
